en: Lightning can and does strike the same place multiple times; the Empire State Building is struck by lightning about 25 times per year.
The far side of the Moon receives just as much sunlight as the near side; we simply cannot see it from Earth because the Moon is tidally locked.
Earth's seasons are caused by the 23.5-degree tilt of its axis, not by how close or far Earth is from the Sun during its orbit.
The Great Wall of China cannot be seen from space with the naked eye, but astronauts in low orbit can see highways, dams, and cities.
A single teaspoon of healthy soil contains billions of living microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, and protozoa that break down organic matter.
Pumice is an igneous rock so full of trapped gas bubbles that it is light enough to float on water.
The Sun is not on fire but produces energy through nuclear fusion, combining hydrogen atoms into helium at temperatures around 15 million degrees Celsius.
Clouds are made of tiny liquid water droplets or solid ice crystals, not water vapor, which is an invisible gas.
Most diamonds formed deep in Earth's mantle from pure carbon under extreme heat and pressure, long before coal or trees even existed.
Tornadoes form over land and are much smaller than hurricanes, which are massive storm systems that form over warm ocean water.
Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
The Moon does not produce any light of its own but shines by reflecting sunlight off its rocky surface.
